stem: When examining a child with a murmur, what should be listened to first before further characterising the murmur?

options.text: The liver edge before the precordium

explanation: Heart sounds should be listened to first. This provides the initial auscultatory information before the murmur is characterised further.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because heart sounds are the first structure to assess on auscultation before analysing the murmur further.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because the apex beat is not the first auscultatory target in a structured murmur examination.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because listening to the carotid arteries alone does not replace assessment of heart sounds in the precordium.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because the liver edge is examined as part of the broader cardiac assessment, not before auscultating heart sounds.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because breath sounds may be relevant in general examination, but they are not the first focus when assessing a murmur.
